newsitem.title: IRAQ: Saddam speech to mark revolution anniversary-INA.
newsitem.headline: Saddam speech to mark revolution anniversary-INA.

text.p: Iraq's President Saddam Hussein will deliver a televised speech on Thursday to mark the 29th anniversary of the revolution which brought his Baath party to power, the Iraqi News Agency INA reported on Wednesday.

It said Saddam would talk about the relationship between Iraq and the United Nations Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of dismantling Iraq's prohibited weapons under the ceasefire terms of the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
UNSCOM must certify Iraq has no such weapons before the U.N. curbs on Iraqi oil exports can be lifted.
Since December the U.N. has allowed Baghdad limited oil sales worth $2 billion to buy urgent needs for Iraqis, suffering from stringent U.N. sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
INA said Saddam would also deal with "relations between Iraq and Turkey and between Turkey and the Arabs and set a formula for consolidated ties which guarantee legitimate interests of all parties".

Turkey sent 10,000 troops into northern Iraq on May 14 in a campaign against Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels who use bases in the mountains to strike against Turkey. Late in June Ankara said it had withdrawn its forces from northern Iraq.
